title: Siloed edge change telemetry and approval hypothesis
summary: Working hypothesis for collecting and surfacing compact, per-customer edge change telemetry that powers short-lived approval gates and fast reconciliation. Focus: customer-managed network changes (firewall rules, peering, cert rotation) where Redwood cannot rely on in-band control plane hooks.
content:
Context:
We get frequent requests from customers who operate their own edge/VPC components and ask Redwood to: 1) require an approval check before we accept a config change (e.g., route/peering update), and 2) keep a searchable audit trail for security/compliance teams. Because the network is customer-managed we can’t always rely on synchronous callbacks or agent-based attestations.

Goal:
Design a lightweight telemetry + approval composition that: 
- produces a compact change "proof" that is easy to transfer and store (low cost for host-based storage)
- allows Redwood to evaluate and gate platform actions with a configurable risk policy
- supports fast reconciliation so discrepancies are surfaced within minutes
- meets basic compliance expectations (immutable-ish, tamper-evident metadata, retention configuration)

Primary user stories:
- Security admin: "I want to see who asked for a VPC route change, what changed, when, and whether Redwood allowed/blocked the operation."
- Operator: "I want automated preflight checks that prevent a model-serving rollout if a customer firewall denies the route."
- Support engineer: "Given a customer outage, I can pull the last 24h change timeline and reconcile what Redwood saw vs. customer netops events."

Design constraints & assumptions:
- We cannot ship an agent to every customer; prefer options that work with common primitives (syslog, s3 uploads, webhook push).
- Many customers use human ticketing flows; change events may be batched or delayed up to ~15 minutes.
- Data minimization: keep payloads compact and avoid shipping full diffs when not needed.

Telemetry model (proposal):
- Change capsule: a small JSON blob that describes a single logical change event. Stored in a compact append-only store (redwood-side). Also allows storing the hash + minimal index if customers prefer to push to their own S3 and give us a signed pointer.
- Capsule fields (example):
  - capsule_id: uuid
  - customer_id: org-123
  - actor: "alice@example.com" (email or service principal)
  - change_type: ROUTE_ADD | ROUTE_DEL | CERT_ROTATE | PEER_UPDATE
  - scope: vpc-id or endpoint-id
  - time_observed: ISO8601
  - source_hint: syslog|s3|webhook|ticketing-link
  - manifest_hash: sha256(hex) (hash of compact representation)
  - ttl: optional short-lived proof expiry (minutes)
  - raw_summary: short human sentence (<= 240 chars)
- Size goal: keep capsule under ~1.5 KB typical. Avoid embedding full config dumps.

Approval gate composition:
- Preflight gate (synchronous): Redwood checks for the existence of a capsule within a lookback window (configurable per customer/route). If found and matches policy, allow. Else: mark as "requires-approval" and optionally stop rollout.
- Async reconciliation gate: Even if preflight allowed, we run reconciliation (compare downstream telemetry within X minutes). If mismatch, trigger rollback or alert depending on severity.

Risk policy sketch (policy DSL):
- allow_if: capsule.exists && capsule.change_type in allow-list && actor in allowlist.roles
- require_secondary_evidence_if: capsule.source_hint == ticketing && change_type == ROUTE_ADD
- fail_closed_after: 2 failed reconciliations -> rollback

Proof transport patterns (we support multiple):
1) Push: customer webhook to our endpoint with capsule payload + signature header.
2) Pull from customer s3: customer writes capsule files to S3 with object naming convention; Redwood uses cross-account read (preferred for large customers).
3) Pull from syslog/forwarder: customer forwards specific lines to our ingest collector with filtering rules.
4) Pull from ticketing: short link + ticket metadata accepted as lower-trust evidence (policy can require stronger evidence).

Integrity & minimal tamper-detection:
- Customers sign capsule payload with their key (optional). At minimum we compute and store sha256 and keep an append-only log with sequence numbers per-customer.
- Make sequence numbers monotonic but allow gaps — we record gaps as part of reconciliation.

Retention & cost model:
- Default retention: 90 days of full capsules, followed by 1 year of compact indices (capsule_id + manifest_hash + timestamp).
- Optional premium: longer retention / immutability window for enterprise customers.

Operational queries & runbook snippets:
- Quick query: "List capsules for org-123 in last 60m where change_type==CERT_ROTATE" -> used during incident triage.
- Reconciliation report job (runs every 5m): fetch latest customer-supplied capsule stream, run diff vs observed platform network events, emit anomalies to ticketing and alerting.
- Runbook: if reconciliation reports anomaly severity >= medium: create incident, notify SRE on-call, and if policy configured, start auto-rollback of recent model rollouts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Ingest pipeline accepts capsules via webhook and S3 with basic validation (schema + manifest_hash).
- Policy engine can evaluate allow/require/deny rules using capsule fields.
- Reconciliation pipeline runs and surfaces anomalies within 10m of observed mismatch.
- Lightweight UI: per-customer timeline view showing capsules + policy evaluation result + reconciliation status.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we prevent customer-supplied "proofs" from being replayed? (Consider nonce/timestamps + short TTL + signed counters.)
- What minimum SLA do we require on ingestion endpoints to be useful for preflight checks?
- Should we offer a small reference agent (python) to customers that produces capsules from common network devices? Good for early adopters.
- Failure modes: what if network latency causes capsule to arrive after preflight window? Need configurable tolerance and graceful "soft-allow" behavior.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Engineering (Marco): prototype webhook + schema validation (2w).
- Product (Asha): finalize policy DSL examples and UI mockups (1w).
- Solutions Eng (Tomás): recruit 2 customers for early feedback and test cross-account S3 ingestion (3w).

Notes to self: keep capsule minimal; avoid convincing legal to call this "immutable evidence" — call it "authenticated telemetry" until we finalize non-replay guarantees.

Appendix: sample capsule (compact):
{
  "capsule_id":"c6f9a8d0-1a3b-4b2f-9e21-0f6a8d7b2d3c",
  "customer_id":"org-123",
  "actor":"alice@example.com",
  "change_type":"ROUTE_ADD",
  "scope":"vpc-abc-1:subnet-22",
  "time_observed":"2025-09-18T15:24:03Z",
  "source_hint":"s3",
  "manifest_hash":"3f4b2a...",
  "raw_summary":"added 10.0.4.0/24 route to gateway gw-12",
  "ttl": 900
}

Feedback welcome — aiming to lock down MVP assumptions before roadmap sync on Oct 6.
